title: Implement warm-pool buffer and probe-delta smoothing for KEDA/HPA to reduce cold-start underprovisioning
creator: Asha Patel
summary: After a capacity regression on 2026-03-08 we observed repeated underprovisioning for short burst traffic where KEDA scaled slowly and HPA reacted to noisy probe metrics. This ticket captures the postmortem conclusions and implements two primary mitigations: a warm-pool of pre-initialized workers and smoothing of probe-derived deltas used by the autoscalers.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-08 03:12 UTC — Spike in burst traffic to hosted inference endpoints in eu-west-1 coinciding with a customer A/B test rollout (INC-2026-03-08-17)
2026-03-08 03:14 UTC — First client errors and elevated 5xx rates observed in runtime-frontend (dashboards: /d/scale-events/eu-west-1)
2026-03-08 03:18 UTC — KEDA scaled based on external scaler metric but new replicas failed readiness checks due to heavy model cold-start (KV cache warmup) causing delayed capacity readiness
2026-03-08 03:25 UTC — HPA observed transient probe noise (probe latency variance and CPU jitter) and trimmed target replica recommendations, leading to sustained underprovisioning for 12 minutes
2026-03-08 03:40 UTC — Emergency mitigation: raise replica lower-bound for affected deployment to 3 and enable temporary synthetic warm calls to populate KV cache
2026-03-08 04:10 UTC — Traffic normalized and incident declared mitigated; follow-up investigation opened
root_cause: The autoscaling decision path relied on a combination of KEDA external scaler metrics and HPA probe-derived deltas that were highly sensitive to probe noise and model cold-start times. Specifically: (1) new replicas required non-trivial model KV cache and kernel JIT warmup causing them to be unavailable for several seconds; (2) KEDA's scaler returned scale recommendations with coarse trampolining that did not account for readiness lag; (3) HPA target calculations used raw probe latency deltas without smoothing, making the controller react to noise and reduce replica counts during the warmup window.
detection: On-call noticed elevated 5xx rate and high 95th-percentile latency for token-generation requests. Alerts triggered from the per-route error-rate policy and the autoscaling mismatch dashboard (alert: autoscale-readiness-mismatch-eu-west-1).
impact: Client-facing 5xx errors and tail-latency increases for ~12 minutes across multiple hosted API routes in eu-west-1; estimated 18k failed tokens and degradation for 2 paying customers during key test windows.
mitigation: Immediate mitigation combined raising minimum replica counts for impacted deployments and running a short-lived synthetic traffic job that calls the model generate endpoint to prepopulate KV caches. We also temporarily switched the external scaler to a higher-sensitivity mode to force quicker scale-up while preserving cost controls.
action_items: Diego — Implement a configurable warm-pool feature in the serving controller: maintain N pre-initialized worker pods per node pool to cover typical cold-starts. Due: 2026-03-26
Priya — Add probe-delta smoothing in the HPA controller: apply exponential moving average to readiness/latency deltas before computing replica recommendations. Due: 2026-03-19
Sam — Modify KEDA external scaler to surface readiness-adjusted recommendations: include expected readiness lag metadata and introduce a recommended 'ramp' window. Due: 2026-03-24
QA — Add e2e test scenario that simulates burst traffic with model cold-starts and verifies that scale decisions avoid transient undershoot. Due: 2026-03-22
Infra — Create a synthetic-warm job template and schedule policy for short prewarming during high-likelihood windows (customer rollouts). Due: 2026-03-15
Observability — Add dashboard panels showing 'replica readiness lag', 'KV cache warmup duration', and 'autoscaler-smoothed-delta' metrics. Due: 2026-03-17
PM/Oncall — Update runbook to include a quick mitigation checklist: (a) raise min replicas, (b) enable synthetic warm calls, (c) flip KEDA sensitivity toggle. Due: 2026-03-14
decisions: Adopt warm-pool approach rather than increasing global minimum replica counts to avoid unnecessary cost increases under normal load.
Introduce smoothing on probe deltas with tunable alpha rather than hard thresholds so that different services can tune aggressively or conservatively.
Prefer readiness-adjusted KEDA recommendations (include expected readiness lag) over immediate scale forcing to reduce oscillation risk.
Treat KV cache warmup as a first-class metric to be exposed to autoscalers and dashboards.
Do not change model container images or quantization as part of this ticket — model warmup optimization is tracked in separate work (ENG-62212).
followups: Measure cost impact of warm-pool at multiple sizes (N=1..5) and compare against baseline min-replica cost; report by 2026-04-02
Roll out probe-delta smoothing to a small set of non-critical services for a 2-week canary before cluster-wide rollout
Coordinate with solutions and customer success to notify customers of reduced risk during scheduled A/B rollouts
Investigate opportunistic background cache transfer between warm workers and new replicas to shorten readiness lag (spike idea).
review_feedback: PM (Lina) — +1 to warm-pool; asked to include cost guardrails and an opt-out label for low-priority services.
Design (Marco) — Requested a compact dashboard widget summarizing current warm pool headroom and projected warming time.
SRE (Ravi) — Suggested adding a per-cluster safety cap and explicit retry windows to synthetic warm calls to avoid causing jitter during network partitions.
Security (Priya K.) — No data-exfil risk identified for synthetic warm calls; recommended using internal-only service account and KMS-wrapped credentials for any remote triggers.
notes: This regression differs from prior 'probe noise' incidents because readiness lag here was dominated by model-internal warmup (KV cache and JIT); prior incidents were primarily HPA metric misconfiguration.
Warm-pool implementation should be pluggable and supported for both hosted and dedicated deployments; Dedicated customers may want ability to opt-in with policy controls.
We expect the combination of warm-pool + smoothing to reduce frequency of transient undershoot incidents by >80% on synthetic tests; verification pending canary.
Keep ENG-62212 (model start-up optimization) and ENG-62418 tightly coordinated — warm-pool is a runtime mitigation while ENG-62212 is an upstream performance improvement.
